The serpent was craftier than any wild animal that YHWH God had made. It said to the woman, “Did God really say, ‘You must not eat from any tree of the garden’?”

Model translations, final opinions and history

Selection rationale: 꾀가 많았다는 비교와 복수 너희를 보존하고, 하나님이 정말로라고 묻는 반문 및 어떤 나무에서도라는 전면 금지 인용을 현재 채택한다.

claude-opus-5-5Now the serpent was shrewder than any wild animal that the LORD God had made. וּמִפְּרִ֣י הָעֵץ֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּתוֹךְ־הַגָּן֒ אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים לֹ֤א תֹֽאכְלוּ֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְלֹ֥א תִגְּע֖וּ בּ֑וֹ פֶּן־תְּמֻתֽוּן׃

But concerning the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, God said, ‘You must not eat from it or touch it, lest you die.’”

Current best selected translation · v0.4.6

Model translations, final opinions and history

Selection rationale: 먹지 말라와 만지지 말라를 여자가 전하는 말로 그대로 보존한다. פן은 피하려는 결과로 옮기며 ממנו는 문맥상 그것에서로 읽는다.

ModelProposed translationFinal opinion — Korean original
gemini-3.8-flash-medium"but of the fruit of the tree that is in the middle of the garden, God said, 'You [plural] shall not eat from it, neither shall you [plural] touch it, lest you [plural] die.'"창세기 2:17의 원명령에 기대어 여자의 발화를 사후 조화시키지 않고, 본문에 기록된 대로 만짐 금지(‘만지지도 말라 / or touch it / ni lo toquen’)를 온전히 보존했습니다. OSHB에서 ‘מִמֶּנּוּ’가 1인칭 복수(1cp)로 오태깅되어 있으나 문맥에 맞게 3인칭 단수 ‘그것을 / from it / de él’로 정확히 번역되었습니다. ‘פֶּן(lest / para que no / 죽지 않도록)’ 역시 여자의 주관적 심리(의심·과장)를 예단하지 않고 행위의 부정적 귀결을 막기 위한 접속사 본연의 통사적 기능대로 번역되었습니다. 다만 한국어의 경우 ‘죽지 않도록 먹지도 만지지도 말라’는 어순으로 인해 접속절이 금지 명령의 사전 목적처럼 읽힐 수 있으므로, ‘먹지도 만지지도 말라. 그렇지 않으면 죽을 것이다/죽지 않도록 하여라’ 형태와의 긴장이 존재합니다.
gpt-6.1-solBut concerning the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, God said, ‘You must not eat from it or touch it, lest you die.’”먹지 말라와 만지지 말라를 여자가 전하는 말로 그대로 보존한다. פן은 피하려는 결과로 옮기며 ממנו는 문맥상 그것에서로 읽는다. 왜 접촉 금지가 앞 장의 기록과 다른지는 확정하지 않는다. 수입 형태분석 1cp 태그는 그대로 남기며, 파라고긱 눈에 필수적인 엄중함을 부여하지 않는다. Gemini가 지적한 목적절 선행의 경고 효과 차이를 기록하되 세 언어의 피하려는 결과라는 현재 선택을 유지한다.

반대 근거: 왜 접촉 금지가 앞 장의 기록과 다른지는 확정하지 않는다. 수입 형태분석 1cp 태그는 그대로 남기며, 파라고긱 눈에 필수적인 엄중함을 부여하지 않는다. 한국어 목적절을 앞에 둔 선택은 경고의 강도를 덜 드러낼 수 있으며, 금지 뒤에 경고를 두는 어순도 대안이다.

EDITORIAL NOTES

Text and translation notes

  1. Verse 1 selects a rhetorical did God really say question, also listed in BDB. Exclamatory or unfinished-speech alternatives remain open. Not from any tree is selected, with not from every tree retained as a scope alternative. The serpent is not identified by an added theological name.
  2. Verses 2–3 are one speech by the woman. The reported do not touch prohibition is retained, without harmonizing it to chapter 2 or assigning blame for the difference. The supplied 1cp tag for ממנו in v. 3 remains in the source analysis; the contextual rendering is from it. Lest expresses an avoided outcome, without settling the speaker’s psychology.
  3. Verses 4–5 are one speech by the serpent. Verse 4 selects certainly will not die while retaining a denial of the certainty of death as an alternative. Immediate death, delay and immortality are not settled by the construction or the final nun.
  4. Like God in v. 5 is the current choice, with like gods/divine beings as an alternative. The first knowing participle is singular and the later one plural; the latter’s attachment remains discussable. BDB lists this verse twice under God, without exhausting syntactic options. The scope of good and evil is not restricted to one doctrinal or biological explanation.
  5. You is plural in vv. 1, 3, 4 and 5; English leaves you uncluttered and explains the plurality here. Spanish uses ustedes forms. Quotation marks, question marks and sentence divisions are editorial, not a transcription of modern punctuation from an ancient manuscript.
  6. Verse 6 selects desirable for gaining wisdom. BDB lists this verse under look at while discussing cognitive alternatives; the visual reading is not disproved. The scope of the third evaluative clause remains discussable. With her does not establish his presence throughout the preceding dialogue.
  7. Verse 7 selects waist coverings. BDB lists girdle and loin-covering for this verse. Sewing leaves does not establish size, cut, complexity or full-body clothing. The supplied singular tag for leaf is preserved; translations express the collective naturally.
  8. Verse 8 selects sound for qol, which can also mean voice, and attaches walking about to God; movement of the sound remains an alternative. The day/evening wind entry in BDB informs the breeze wording, without fixing time, temperature, direction, storm or a daily habit. Breeze is a translation choice, not a verified wind strength.
  9. Verse 9 selects the man and singular you; Adam remains a naming alternative, without a universal rule from the article alone. Verse 10 is his first-person answer. Sound/voice alternatives remain; Spanish Te oí leaves the noun sound implicit. Present nakedness and English/Spanish past-tense backshift are rendering choices; guilt, repentance, clothing effectiveness and a fixed chronology are not added.
